en: And tear her limb from limb!
Slaughter her giant Ulukman,
Gouge out his eyes and blind him!
Close in from every side,
And thrust your spears all together.
Plunge into turmoil and battle
And take this bitch’s life!
My intimates and confidants,
My companions who grew up beside me,
Who shared adventures with me,
Who joined me in hunting argali,
Who rode on raids with me,
Who walked beside me
Into the seething ranks of foes,
Facing the dire bullets meant for me!
She is molded like pure wheat dough,
Slender as a white gazelle;
Unable to spear this bitch,
My tiny soul has burned away.
My spear bent at my waist,
And such force has come upon my body
That my spine aches,
My right ribs have folded,
And ruinous pain has struck my head.
My sight has dimmed and my strength is gone;
After jousting with such mighty force,
The ill-fated bitch of a champion
Has shown her stubbornness.
She stretched forth and struck once with her spear,
And Sarybay despaired of life.
His insides burned like embers;
Nothing like it had been seen in the world.
Sarybay was shattered to pieces
And seemed utterly consumed.
My dear champions,
Comrades who share death with me,
Companions gathered in life,
Faithful mourners if I depart,
Stand not idle—thrust your spears!
Friends dearer than brothers,
Ever since I became Sarybay,
Ever since Sarybay mounted a horse,
I have worn a golden crown.”
Then Sarybay,
Roaring menacingly,
Sat astride his horse with legs spread wide.
“I have seen countless holy wars and conflicts,
And never died amid their seething tumult.
Never upon the earth have I seen
A calamity like this warrior girl.
Swarm over her from every side!
The work of the many is a lake, a river—
Stand not idle; level your spears!
Stand not idle; unleash the battle!
Rescue your falcon, Sarybay,
And bear him away!
Confidants who heed my words,
Companions who restore life to me,
Men who stand beneath my banner,
Men ready to sacrifice their lives!”
When Sarybay had spoken thus,
The vast host surged forward;
Such is the way of a general mêlée.
Arrows filled the air like rain;
Those whose appointed death had truly come
Fell to the shafts and boiled in misery.
The earth was torn apart and night descended;
Think of it—a day of calamity had come.
With frenzied snarling,
Musket balls whistled,
And arrows from bows flashed;
Wherever they struck, bodies burst apart,
Blood poured in streams,
And the gnawed earth was gouged into hollows.
Every person they met was slaughtered,
Sarybay’s countless host,
When their khan gave the command,
Swept over the land that day.
The maiden Kuyaly, lion-hearted girl,
While they swarmed like ants,
They surged up and surrounded her,
Thrusting spears and shouting,
Each of them a grave menace,
Raising the cry of “Sarybay!”
When their numbers overwhelmed her,
The earth was churned into dust,
As they closed in and encircled her,
The ground sagged beneath the massed host,
The maiden Kuyaly, the champion,
As they were about to trap her in their midst,
A roar arose upon their flank,
A clamor splitting the sky,
His warriors and lions,
His champions and heroes,
Those most skillful with the spear,
Those strongest at devising stratagems,
Brave Seytek, the hero’s son,
Was coming forth with his chosen men,
The swiftest fierce as ogres,
Swooping like hawks upon their targets,
Brave Seytek, the hero’s son,
Was driving them forward.
Stretching out all who faced him,
He came steadily onward.
“If fate has come, I shall die,” he said,
“For the champion maiden Kuyaly,
I shall stand as her protector,” he said,
Brave Seytek, son of the lion,
Drove back all who crowded upon him,
Spearing heroes on the slope,
Piercing many in succession,
His spears split the army apart.
By the time the hero’s son arrived,
Broad in spirit as Talas,
In stature the image of Manas,
In judgment the equal of Koshoy,
Charging like a wild boar,
The way he cleaved through their ranks
Was like a winter blizzard.
Terrified at the sight of this,
Sarybay, son of an ogre,
Found no deep grave in which to hide,
No friendly host to flee toward,
As the dark army poured in,
That was how they faced one another.
Standing face-to-face,
Firing guns and drawing bows,
They fought with wet, crushing blows,
Clashing their spears,
Raising a fearsome tumult,
The armies met and uproar rose,
Host crashed against host,
They hammered one another,
May God never show us such a sight,
The tasseled standards seethed aloft,
Their battle cries became a mighty roar,
Such was the dreadful struggle,
When the armies confronted each other,
And waged battle without yielding,
Baring their great teeth,
Horses died until mountains were blocked,
Mustaches bristled,
Corpses of heroes rose like hills,
Many mortals there beheld
The journey from which none return,
Drenched in crimson blood,
Many mortals lay dying.
It was a grievous, mighty conflict,
The people were slaughtered without mercy.
Spears shattered and lashings fell,
Corpses of heroes formed mountains,
An immeasurable slaughter took place.
The hollow filled with crimson blood,
Deep ravines filled with corpses.
The souls of the living burned with anguish,
And whoever looked upon that age
Saw its falseness revealed,
All scattered in confusion,
Crushing without respite
Those they had marked for their ranks,
Engaged in riotous slaughter.
Many a splendid warhorse,
Wandered riderless and bare of saddle.
Many a fleet courser,
Neighed while dragging its reins,
Its riderless heart grieving.
It was a dreadful, mighty conflict,
Many among the people witnessed it,
And many mortals lay dying.
All the warriors trembled,
The people cried out one by one,
Thrusting and fencing with spears,
They kept slaughtering one another,
The great conflict tightened its coils,
Becoming a chaos beyond understanding,
As they continued their strife,
A terrible massacre took place.
When Sarybay’s troops saw brave Seytek’s bearing,
They surrendered,
Some heroes after others,
Their knees buckling,
Ran after him and bowed,
Taking reins knotted with loops,
And hanging them around their necks,
While one man from another
Contended to offer him a warhorse.
Hurrying and trotting forward,
They came as envoys,
Submitting to the hero,
And vying to offer livestock.
They began according to ancient custom,
And thus brought the fighting
And conflict to an end.
The two armies that had clashed
Made peace that day,
They began speaking to one another,
Gathered their wits and opened counsel,
And began their sorrowful plea:
“Because of what has happened,
Because of Sarybay,
We became an army tens of thousands strong,
And the whole world was stirred.
Sarybay drove us here,
Though he had neither rope nor cord,
Sarybay brought us here in bonds.
He unleashed his terrible wrath,
And even before Saikal’s many daughters-in-law
Could look back toward their village,
We suffered misery and innocent deaths,
Though our livestock had grazed freely,
And men despaired of life.
The cause of their despair
Was an army vast as a hearth-fire,
Which devastated the people without respite.
A tyrant named Sarybay arose,
Gathering the people and mustering an army,
Amassing the entire host in abundance.
When his khan gave the command,
He stiffened and poured out his fury,
And while he stood enraged,
Could the Saruu voice any grievance?
When your lord bellows from his throne,
Is there a horse among the people that a camel could stop?
Not a single head of livestock remained in the pens,
Nor strength remained to turn and flee,
Not a shod yearling remained,
Not a living soul among the born remained.
He began such outrages,
And anyone who resisted
He slaughtered without leaving one alive.
He committed notorious atrocities,
And brought every mortal low.
Seizing his moment, he scattered us,
Raging and shouting,
Bringing calamity upon mankind,
Sarybay drove us here.
When he carried out his massacre,
Saying, ‘Do as I command,’
Sarybay brought us as his chosen force.
The black halter of the fugitives
Sarybay brought concealed.
Our precious heads into calamity
Sarybay brought entangled.
While the people lived in freedom,
Hunting deer when they grew weary,
And when they were not weary, the dear people
Delighting in great festivities,
Sharing joy together,
While many peoples lived happily,
He brought such strife upon the nation,
And revealed horrors never seen by man.
The warriors’ misery boiled over,
As though struck by a plague of turmoil,
He drove souls onward without rest.
The infidel son of an ogre
Was seized by his thirst for blood.
